<cite ref="Onkelos Leviticus 23:43">Targ. O. ib. 43</cite> <cite ref="M01017"><he>מְטַלַּת</he></cite> (Ms. I <cite ref="M01009"><he>מְטָלָיוּת</he></cite>, III <cite ref="M01017"><he>מְטַלַּת</he></cite> pl.).
Targ. Is. IV, 6.—Esp. festive booth, Succah.

<cite ref="Sukkah 3a">Succ. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>אפומא דמטלל׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <cite ref="M00984"><he>מטולתא</he></cite>, <he>מטלתא</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) at the entrance of the Succah. Ib. 28ᵇ <he>במ׳</he> in the Succah, <he>בר ממ׳</he> without the Succah (in the house &c.).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:2:2">Y. M. Kat. III, 82ᵃ</cite> <he>הוות מְטַלְּתֵיה וכ׳</he> if his (the mourner’s) Succah is small; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Tractate Semachot 11:16">Treat. S’maḥ. ch. XI</cite>, end <he>מטלתא דכרמא</he> the watchman’s hut in the vineyard—a mistaken gloss to <cite ref="A00561"><he>אודייני</he></cite>, which found its way into the text; v.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 27a">M. Kat. 27ᵃ</cite>, a. <cite ref="A00891"><he>אוּרְיָינִי</he></cite>.]—Pl. <cite ref="M01018"><he>מְטַלָּתָא</he></cite>, <cite ref="M01000"><he>מְטַלָּן</he></cite>. Targ. O. Lev. l. c., v. supra.
